elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 3.2 as rendered retains automatic renewal ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term") and the conditional automatic-renewal elements below (12-month cap, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, CPI/3% cap) are not all satisfied, so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal term remains "equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment"; no 12-month ceiling was inserted, so a Service Option Attachment with an initial term over 12 months would auto-renew for that longer period.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires written notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out window.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No IBM reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; the comment does not add one either.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap is "will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term" (5%), not the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 3.2 now reads "unless either party gives the other party written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 60 days, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a pattern-match artifact caused by the drafter's rewording of "notifies the other party in writing" to "gives the other party written notice"; substantively the 60-day figure is present in the operative text.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: New operative sentence: "Charges for each renewal term will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term of the applicable Service Option Attachment." This is an unconditional 5% ceiling on each renewal uplift; Section 13.1's change right is a general notice-based change mechanic and does not by its terms authorise renewal charges above the specific cap.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the non-renewal window is cut from ninety (90) to sixty (60) days and renewal charges are capped at 105% of the prior term, so both fallback elements are met in operative language and the 'deviation' classification with a fallback-targeted redline is correct.

Minimality defect: the edit paraphrases wording outside the target element — original "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior" was rewritten as "unless either party gives the other party written notice at least sixty (60) days prior". Only the numeral needed to change. Repair by restoring the original construction: "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term...". This cosmetic rewrite is also what caused the deterministic notice-window regex to report 'number not found'.

Preferred level fails on four counts if we later escalate: (i) no 12-month ceiling on the renewal term (it still tracks the previous term's duration); (ii) opt-out notice is 60 days, not 30; (iii) no IBM obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal; (iv) uplift cap is 5%, not the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Intent is preserved: Section 13.1's change right, the non-retroactivity sentence and Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election all survive, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling. For belt-and-braces, consider opening the new cap sentence with "Notwithstanding Section 13.1," only if IBM argues its price-change right overrides the renewal cap — as drafted the specific renewal cap should control, so the added words are not required.
